No — not at that time and location.

Your app’s Moon altitude of **−31.3°** means the Moon is about 31° *below* the geometric horizon. That is far too far below for atmospheric refraction, terrain effects, or any ordinary observational uncertainty to matter. Even unusually strong refraction near the horizon only shifts objects by roughly a degree or so, not tens of degrees.

The Moon’s 11% illumination and clear, dark sky would matter if it were above the horizon, but they cannot overcome being that far below it. You would need to wait until moonrise; at 02:39 UTC it is decisively on the other side of the Earth from your local sky.
